sources.label: Launch
sources.note: Direct HASI release supports the partnership mandate, initial commitments, HASI role and KKR Core Infrastructure attribution.

sources.label: 2024 10-K note
sources.note: SEC filing supports the two 50% members, governance, service arrangements and seed-asset mechanics.

sources.label: 2025 notes
sources.note: Direct release supports the $592mm senior-notes financing and investment-vehicle framing.

sources.label: 2025 upsize
sources.note: Direct release supports the additional $500mm commitment by each partner and nearly $5bn target capacity.

sources.label: 2026 notes
sources.note: Direct release supports the May 2026 second notes issuance and continued vehicle activity.

sources.label: 2026 Q2 10-Q
sources.note: Current SEC filing supports 50/50 ownership, funded commitments, asset and debt balances, investment-period end and continuing active status.

conclusion: Direct HASI and SEC evidence consistently describes CCH1 as a jointly governed investment and financing vehicle holding a mix of project interests, receivables and debt securities, with affiliate service providers rather than a standalone operating workforce or customer business. It therefore fails the manager-level operating PortCo boundary despite remaining active.
